answer: A trellis of peer attestations then grows only when shards match, so faking one identity costs a full stake plus repeated shard proofs. Each agent must stake a unique signed quill mark that a prism splits into per-epoch shards, binding identity to costly work. Sybils multiply stake and proof costs faster than any reward, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
